messages:
Incident Bot: PAGE: control-plane elevated 5xx rate targeting auth/org-lookup/billing — customer-facing 502/504 spike. Paging Aisha (oncall) and SREs. :rotating_light:
Aisha (oncall): I'm awake, joining. Any customer-facing impact metrics?
Tom (sre): seeing global 5xx rate up ~12% over baseline on ingress gateway. Top service = auth-proxy -> org-lookup (timeouts), then config-service (500s). Traces show tail latencies at 2.5s and many retries. Link: https://wavefront/redwood/alerts/172345
Priya (eng): I can pull traces. Running quick query on jaeger: span auth-proxy -> org-lookup.timeouts
Aisha (oncall): Priya, can you confirm if it's a cache stampede on org-lookup? We rolled TTL yesterday.
Priya (eng): Running curl to a node:
```
curl -sv 'https://org-lookup.internal/v1/lookup?id=acct_123' -H 'x-service:auth-proxy'
* Connected to org-lookup (10.2.3.14) port 443 (#0)
< HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout
```
Priya (eng): hitting a few nodes with consistent 504s.
Nina (support): Support reports customers seeing upload errors and API calls returning 502 - multiple tickets opening. Cc @sales for urgent comms.
Tom (sre): quick telemetry: auth-proxy 5xx correlated with a surge of cache-miss DB calls to org-db. db connections spiking. Might be org-lookup losing cache after our recent config TTL change.
Aisha (oncall): Action plan: 1) apply emergency circuit breaker on auth-proxy to fail fast for org-lookup (reduce retries), 2) roll back TTL change in config-service, 3) route a % traffic to standby org-lookup cluster if healthy.
Priya (eng): I'm on circuit-breaker PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/782 — adding cb rule to auth-proxy config. Pushing now.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: auth-proxy/cb-rule v0.2 -> staging
Tom (sre): Applying temporary rate limit on auth-proxy to reduce db pressure: `kubectl patch configmap auth-proxy-rate -p '{"data":{"burst":"50"}}'`
Priya (eng): Rollback plan: `kubectl set env deployment/config-service TTL_OVERRIDE=300` to restore previous TTL.
Aisha (oncall): Priya, proceed with CB and TTL rollback. Tom, apply rate limit and monitor.
Priya (eng): CB deployed to production edge in 45s. Logs:
```
[info] cb tripped for org-lookup node 10.2.3.14 -> fail-fast enabled
```
Tom (sre): Rate limit patched. db connection count dropping. 5xx rate decreasing from 12% -> 4% over past 2 min.
Nina (support): support-dashboard shows ticket volume stabilizing. Customers still affected but fewer errors.
Aisha (oncall): Rolling TTL rollback now.
Priya (eng): TTL override applied. Config-service pods showing healthy. org-lookup cache hit-rate rising from 10% -> 70%.
Tom (sre): 5xx at ingress back to ~1.2% near baseline. Some 504 residuals on old clients still retrying.
Aisha (oncall): Good. Evidence collected: traces, wavefront graphs, logs saved to incident bucket s3://redwood-incidents/1723456789. Notable cause = TTL regression + retry amplification -> DB connection exhaustion -> org-lookup timeouts -> auth-proxy 5xx cascade.
Priya (eng): Root cause: unintended TTL change landed in config rollout 2026-03-13 which reduced cache duration drastically under load pattern X.
Nina (support): Support will update affected customers with a short note. Sales looped in.
Aisha (oncall): Handoff: I'm going offline in 15m. Tom will take oncall for follow-up; Priya will lead postmortem and rollback verification. Next steps: postmortem draft, metric alerts tightened (CB tripping threshold), add canary for future TTL changes.
Tom (sre): taking over. I'll watch for recurrence and confirm ticket triage.
Priya (eng): I'll start postmortem doc and include measurement of the amplification factor + fix: add config change canary and automated load test on TTLs.
deploy-bot: incident annotated: deploys affected: config-service:rollout/2026-03-13
Aisha (oncall): Thanks team. Incident status: mitigated, customer-facing errors decreased. If anything spikes, ping #oncall immediately. :thumbsup:
